ud4.1:3.2: Sitting to one side, Venerable Meghiya said to the Buddha,
ud4.1:4.1: “Sir, I robed up in the morning and, taking my bowl and robe, entered Jantu village for alms.
ud4.1:4.2: After the meal, on my return from almsround in Jantu village, I went to the shore of Kimikālā River.
ud4.1:4.3: Sir, as I was going for a walk along the shore of the river I saw a lovely and delightful mango grove.
ud4.1:4.4: Seeing this, it occurred to me,
ud4.1:4.5: ‘Oh, this mango grove is lovely and delightful!
ud4.1:4.6: This is good enough for striving for a gentleman wanting to strive.
ud4.1:4.7: If the Buddha allows me, I’ll come back to this mango grove to meditate.’
ud4.1:10.2: “Sir, while I was meditating in that mango grove I was beset mostly by three kinds of bad, unskillful thoughts, namely,
ud4.1:10.6: I’ve gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness,
ud4.1:10.7: but I’m still harassed by these three kinds of bad, unskillful thoughts:
